That is NOT the observed mobile profile (390 / DSF 3 / touch / mobile UA), so numbers at 390 here are not directly comparable to the published mobile fidelity numbers. visibleNodeDefinition: An element counts as VISIBLE when ALL hold: (1) computed display !== 'none'; (2) it participates in layout — offsetParent !== null, OR computed position is 'fixed'/'sticky', OR it is <html>/<body>; (3) getBoundingClientRect() has width > 0 AND height > 0. hiddenNodeCount = totalElements - visibleNodeCount, where totalElements = document.querySelectorAll('*').length. Consequence recorded on purpose: display:contents wrappers (the clone's .wr-variant / .wr-svg-host / .wr-nest, and any source equivalent) generate no box and are therefore counted as HIDDEN on both sides; displayContentsCount is reported separately so the count can be read either way. This also means the clone's hiddenNodeCount is structurally ~2x the source's, because the clone ships BOTH observed viewport trees in one document and hides one — hiddenNodeCount is therefore only comparable ACROSS WIDTHS ON THE SAME SIDE, never clone-vs-source. displayNoneCount is the cross-side-comparable channel.

pricingTableProbe.what: 28.5A reported that inside the 1024-1231.98px synthetic @media band the clone's /pricing plan-comparison table loses its header row and three of four plan columns. This probe counts VISIBLE leaf elements whose exact text is a plan name, on both sides, at 5 widths.
pricingTableProbe.note: The comparison table is a CSS grid of <div>s, not a <table> — visibleTables is 0 on both sides at every width, so plan-name occurrences are the addressable proxy. A count of 1 per plan means only the plan CARDS are shown; 2 (3 for Enterprise) means the comparison table's header row is present too.
pricingTableProbe.verdict: The clone's comparison table appears only at >=1232px; the live source's appears by 1100px. 914 and 1024 AGREE (both narrow) — so the band's LOWER edge is right and its UPPER edge (1231.98) overshoots the source's real transition, which lies in (1024, 1100]. At 1100 the clone shows 1 of 4 plan columns and no header row, and carries 286 fewer characters of visible text than the source (2351 vs 2637). 28.5A measured 274 characters lost in the same band; 286 today is the same defect at the same magnitude, not a new one.
pricingTableProbe.manualInspectionNote: Manually inspected crop-table-source-1100.png vs crop-table-clone-1100.png (y 1380..1780 of each full-page capture). SOURCE: a header row reading 'Features | Free | Basic | Business | Enterprise' followed by four populated value columns. CLONE: no header row at all, and only the first value column (Unlimited / 10MB / 250 issues / 2 teams) — Basic, Business and Enterprise are absent, with their space left as empty background. At 1440 the two crops match. This reproduces 28.5A's description exactly.

stylesheetResidual.what: The mechanism 28.5A named, re-counted in the SHIPPED hardened artifact.
stylesheetResidual.note: Every one of the 738 @media blocks in the generated stylesheet is at that single synthetic band; the sheet contains no other breakpoint. app/globals.css adds the 914.98/915 variant switch (2 blocks). 28.5A counted 710 blocks with 709 at the same band. Wave-1 did not remove, narrow or widen this mechanism — it is intact.
stylesheetResidual.variantSwitch: app/globals.css: [data-wr-viewport='desktop'] display:none under (max-width: 914.98px); [data-wr-viewport='mobile'] display:none under (min-width: 915px). Breakpoint 915 is inferred (observed-endpoint midpoint of 390 and 1440), not observed.

391-914 dead zone.finding285A: at 391-914px all 8 routes render as a 390px column pinned to the left of the canvas; the clone stranded a 390px column on a 914px canvas (/pricing scrollHeight 7712 vs live 6990).
391-914 dead zone.evidenceNow: All 8 of 8 routes produce a frozen-band discontinuity spanning 390..914: scrollHeight, visibleNodeCount, displayNoneCount and visibleTextLength are BIT-IDENTICAL at 390, 500, 700 and 914 on every route. On 5 routes (/, /customers, /plan, /pricing, /security) even maxContentRight is constant; on the other 3 (/changelog, /customers/automattic, /integrations) the ONLY thing that changes across the band is the far edge of a full-bleed element tracking the canvas — the content column itself never moves. <main> stays at its observed 390px width at 500, 700 and 914 on all 8 routes (landmark-collapse), while the live source's <main> tracks the viewport exactly (500 -> 500, 700 -> 700, 914 -> 914). /pricing clone scrollHeight at 914 is 7714 against a live 6990 — 28.5A measured 7712 vs 6990, a 2px difference attributable to source drift, so the defect is numerically UNCHANGED. Visual proof: sweep/crop-hero-clone-914.png shows the 390px column with ~524px of empty canvas to its right; sweep/crop-hero-source-914.png shows a full-width 914px layout.
391-914 dead zone.worseCheck: NOT worse. The frozen band has the same edges (390..914), the same stranded width (390px), and the same scrollHeight (7714 vs 7712, +2px from source drift). No route gained a new dead zone and no route's dead zone widened.
391-914 dead zone.improvedCheck: NOT improved. There is still zero continuous reflow anywhere between 390 and 914 on any of the 8 routes.

1024-1231 pricing band.finding285A: at 1024-1231px /pricing hides 507 nodes and the comparison table loses its header row and three of four plan columns; 274 characters of the plan-comparison table are deleted at every width from 1024 to 1231.98px.
1024-1231 pricing band.evidenceNow: /pricing clone displayNoneCount goes 240 (1440) -> 743 (1024 and 1100), i.e. 503 extra nodes hidden inside the band against 28.5A's 507 — the same mechanism at the same magnitude. visibleNodeCount drops 1706 -> 1035 (-39.3%). Visible text falls 2675 chars (1232) -> 2351 chars (1100), i.e. 286 characters lost against the source's 2637 at the same width (28.5A: 274). The plan-name probe shows the clone at 1 column / no header at 1100 while the source has the full 4-column header row. The 738 synthetic @media blocks producing this are still in the shipped stylesheet.
1024-1231 pricing band.worseCheck: NOT worse. 503 hidden nodes vs 507; 286 lost characters vs 274 (both against a source captured 6 days later, which accounts for the small drift). The band's edges are unchanged.
1024-1231 pricing band.improvedCheck: PARTIALLY REFRAMED, not improved. This sweep adds an edge measurement 28.5A did not have: at 1024 the LIVE SOURCE is also in its narrow layout (source visibleNodeCount 1050 vs clone 1035; plan counts agree exactly), so the band's LOWER edge at 1024 is approximately CORRECT. The defect is entirely in the UPPER edge: the source transitions to the wide comparison layout somewhere in (1024, 1100], while the clone holds the narrow layout until 1232. The mis-served range is therefore ~1100-1231 rather than the full 1024-1231. This is a sharper description of the SAME defect, not a reduction of it — at 1100 the visible loss is total (3 of 4 columns plus the header row).

clone-vs-source screenshot fidelity acro.evidenceNow: /pricing @16 by width: 390 0.0371, 500 0.0387, 700 0.0446, 914 0.0376, 1024 0.0378, 1100 0.0430, 1440 0.0158, 1920 0.0125. The two OBSERVED-adjacent widths (1440, 1920) are 2.4-3.6x better than every un-observed width. commonAreaRatio collapses to 0.9061 at 914 (clone 7714 vs source 6990) and 0.9099 at 1024 (clone 6360 vs source 6990) — the two widths where the clone is on the wrong side of a breakpoint. This is the 28.5A shape (fidelity is only defended where the site was observed) reproduced with photographs at widths 28.5A explicitly said were never photographed.
clone-vs-source screenshot fidelity acro.worseCheck: NOT worse at the observed widths: @1440 @16 is 0.0158, identical to the 28.5B attribution run's post-Wave-1 number (0.0158, down from the pre-Wave-1 0.0295). Wave-1's gains at observed widths are intact and no un-observed width shows a regression signature (all lie in a narrow 0.037-0.045 band consistent with the un-reflowed layout, not with a new defect).

comparisonWith285A.overall: SAME DEFECT, NOT WORSE, NOT FIXED. Wave-1 improved per-pixel fidelity at the observed widths (1440/1920) and left the responsive mechanism — the 915px variant switch plus 738 synthetic 1024-1231.98px @media blocks — completely intact. Every 28.5A responsive finding reproduces at the same magnitude within source-drift noise. Nothing in this document should be read as a responsive fix.

anomalies: HORIZONTAL OVERFLOW IS PARTLY REAL, NOT PURELY A CLONE DEFECT. At 390 the LIVE SOURCE also overflows: /pricing source maxContentRight 1280.47 vs clone 1288.79, and / source-side overflow is present too. linear.app genuinely runs horizontally-scrolling elements at narrow widths. The clone-specific part is that this overflow PERSISTS unchanged to 914 (clone 1288.79) while the source snaps to the viewport (source maxContentRight 914 at 914). Any 28.5C claim about 'content off-canvas' must separate these two.

/customers and /customers/automattic get SHORTER when the desktop variant engages: /customers scrollHeight 8049 (390-914) -> 4886 (>=1024), /customers/automattic 6320 -> 5242. These are legitimate variant switches, not losses, but they trip the >25% scrollHeight-cliff rule and must not be read as content deletion.

/security clone maxContentRight reaches 3348.99 at a 1920 viewport (and 2938.99 at 1100) — ~1429px of content beyond the canvas at 1920, the largest horizontal overflow in the corpus. No live-source counterpart was captured for /security in this task, so whether the source does the same is UNVERIFIED.

The live source's own /changelog scrollHeight is not monotonic across widths (24482 @390, 23636 @500, 24253 @700, 26267 @914, 25657 @1024, 25308 @1100, 25342 @1440) — a lazily-populated feed measured without scrolling. Clone-vs-source height deltas on /changelog therefore carry real source noise and should not be attributed to the clone.

The clone's /pricing at 1440 has scrollHeight 6360 and the source 6360 — exact. At 1024 the clone is 6360 and the source 6990: the clone is 630px SHORT because it has already switched to the desktop variant while the source has not. Both a too-tall (914) and a too-short (1024) failure exist within 110px of each other.

Zero page errors across all 64 clone sweep loads. Console errors are zero on 7 of 8 routes; /customers reports exactly 24 at EVERY width (12 cross-origin CORS-blocked customer-logo SVGs on webassets.linear.app, each producing a CORS message plus a net::ERR_FAILED). Width-invariant, therefore an ASSET-INDEPENDENCE residual, not a responsive one — recorded here only so the 24 is not later mistaken for a responsive failure.

runHygiene.processAnomaly: HONEST DISCLOSURE: two FOREIGN processes, pid 53338 (`pnpm start --port 3212`) and its child pid 53352 (next-server v16.3.3), were alive at the start of this task and were gone by the end. They were never targeted: the only kill issued in this task was an explicit `kill 61800 61773` against two of THIS task's own orphaned next-server processes (identified first by `lsof` cwd = tmp/wr285b/sweep/app), and both foreign pids were verified alive immediately after that kill and again after the clone sweep completed. They disappeared at some point during the live-source sweep or the table probe. No signal was sent to them and the system log shows no jetsam record; the most likely cause is memory pressure from the large full-page captures (/changelog full-page PNGs run to ~26,000 px tall). The other foreign process, pid 24704, survived the whole run.

notes: Read hiddenNodeCount only across widths on one side (the clone ships two viewport trees, the source one). displayNoneCount and visibleTextLength are the cross-side-comparable channels. Screenshot verdicts should be read on @16 and dE76>10, never @1. Nothing here was fixed, and no correction was attempted: this document exists so 28.5C can decide what responsive behaviour the engine should target, with the residual measured rather than assumed.
